title: The Basics of Growth Marketing: Engagement & Retention

reader_summary.headline: So you found product market fit and you're starting to acquire users.
reader_summary.overview: So you found product market fit and you're starting to acquire users. But it's not enough to just have users. You need to make sure they're sticking around and keep finding value in your product. Because as products and platforms evolve over time, so do the users, some of whom may even use the product in different ways.

key_points.text: So what does that mean for engagement and retention?
key_points.evidence_quote: So what does that mean for engagement and retention?

key_points.text: This episode from August 2018 is part two and a two-part series on the basics of growth with two longtime experts.
key_points.evidence_quote: This episode from August 2018 is part two and a two-part series on the basics of growth with two longtime experts, A16Z general partners Andrew Chen and Jeff Jordan, interviewed by Sonal Choxi.

key_points.text: Their discussion covers everything from how network effects come into play.
key_points.evidence_quote: Their discussion covers everything from how network effects come into play, and if there's really a magic number or a ha moment for a product, to who are the power users and the power user curve for measuring, finding, and retaining them.

key_points.text: For more in user acquisition and the basics of growth, check out last week's episode, the first part of this series.
key_points.evidence_quote: For more in user acquisition and the basics of growth, check out last week's episode, the first part of this series.

thesis: The episode argues that after achieving product-market fit and acquiring users, companies must focus on engagement and retention to ensure users continue to find value as the product and user demographics evolve. It explains that successful companies typically progress from an initial focus on acquisition to addressing churn and retention, and eventually to resurrecting users, with cohort analysis serving as a key method to measure these trends and identify network effects.
